integrity: The argument is symbolic. It uses the exact unit-ball, linear-span, and scalar-factor norm descriptions from the focal source and elementary Banach-lattice inequalities; no numerical experiment, exhaustive search, or independence claim is used.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats finite free products and the exponent range \(1<p<\infty\); it does not address countably infinite free products or the endpoint \(p=\infty\).
The sharp universal coefficient is proved when every factor has upper-\(p\) estimate constant at most \(1\); no optimal formula for unequal factor constants is claimed.
A residual originality risk remains for an equivalent older categorical formulation under different terminology.
title: Sharp finite-factor upper-\(p\) estimate constant for Banach-lattice free products
